architecture.title: Four layers of a claw, and the tool that measures each
architecture.caption: Benchmark each layer on its own (research tutorial Part 5.1). The engine is measured with vLLM's built-in `vllm bench serve` (tok/s, TTFT, single stream and a concurrency sweep). The workflow and its quality are measured with `nat eval` and the NAT profiler (p50/p95 runtime, LLM calls and tokens per turn, evaluator scores). The sandbox tax is the p95 difference between the same eval on the host and inside OpenShell. Harnesses without a NAT profiler (Hermes, OpenClaw) are timed through their own API. `nat sizing calc` turns p95-vs-concurrency into a rough GPU (= Spark) count.

sequence.title: One `nat eval` run with the profiler on
sequence.caption: NAT reads the jsonl dataset (question = input, answer = reference), runs the workflow for each row up to max_concurrency at a time, records every LLM and tool event, then writes the profiler files and the evaluator scores. On NAT 1.9.0 each evaluator writes <evaluator key>_output.json. `nat sizing calc` repeats this run once per concurrency value and fits p95 against concurrency.

charts.title: Spark single-stream decode — third-party figures
charts.caption: Third-party measurements quoted in the research tutorial (Part 5.2), each from one machine on one software version: ai-muninn, the NVIDIA developer forum, Exxact's agent benchmark and Exxact's engine comparison. They are reference points to reproduce on your Spark, not specifications, and not this course's measurements. Values marked ~ or + are shown at their stated figure.

charts.title: Spark aggregate throughput under concurrency — third-party figures
charts.caption: Aggregate figures as quoted in the research tutorial: 786 and ~400 tok/s per ai-muninn, >300 (drawn at 300) and ~122 tok/s per Exxact's engine comparison. Exercise 06 divides 786 by 16 sessions: about 49 tok/s each, because batching raises the total, not each stream.

charts.title: Naive single-stream ceiling for a 3B-active MoE at 273 GB/s
charts.caption: Arithmetic from lab 06-1 (clawkit.decode_ceiling_tok_s: bandwidth ÷ bytes of active weights per token, NVFP4 at ~4.5 bits with scales). It is an upper bound: KV-cache reads, non-expert layers and below-peak bandwidth pull real decode lower. ai-muninn, cited in the research tutorial, puts the practical ceiling for this model class in the low 80s tok/s.

charts.title: LAPTOP STAND-IN — Ollama sweep on this Mac (gemma3:4b)
charts.caption: Measured by lab 06-1 on this Mac (laptop Ollama, gemma3:4b, 96-token answers, 2/2/4 requests; TTFT p50 57 ms → 1120 ms → 3188 ms). The aggregate did not rise: this Ollama queued the requests, and other labs may have shared it. It shows the METHOD only and must not be compared with the Spark figures in the other charts.
